correctness.rationale: The source program explicitly generates all matchings of the complement of each labeled cycle n=3..9 and creates every signed simplicial boundary in increasing edge order. The source elimination chooses only unit ±1 pivots and applies integer row and column additions, clearing a pivot row and column without divisions; zero residual proves all nonzero Smith invariant factors are units. This saturates each boundary image in the corresponding free chain lattice, hence integral homology is torsion-free. At n9 f0..f3=(27,216,555,324), boundary ranks r1,r2,r3=(26,190,323); the exact kernel-minus-image rank formulas give b2=42, b3=1, and vanish in other nonnegative degrees. Earlier cases give n5..n7 only Htilde1=Z^1,Z^6,Z^1 and n8 Htilde2=Z^42; n3 empty and n4 simplex. Independent generation and mod2 matrix elimination confirmed the f-vectors, ranks and Betti numbers n3..9; mod2 corroboration alone would not exclude integral torsion, which depends on the inspected unimodular integer algorithm.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General complete-graph and complete bipartite matching-complex homology theorems do not imply exact homology of the proper subcomplex obtained by deleting the cycle edges: deletion may change kernels and attaching maps. The C9 strong discrete Morse complex has different vertices/faces and Htilde4 rank five, not a dominating formula for this anti-hole complex.

value.rationale: The complement-of-cycle (antihole) family is canonical and occurs naturally when forbidding cyclic nearest-neighbor edges in graph matchings. The first occurrence of integral homology in two adjacent positive degrees, including the exact rank-42 H2 and rank-one H3, is a sharp complete finite cutoff that signals new topology beyond one-degree patterns. These are precise reusable invariants, not an arbitrary sample, and no stronger homotopy wedge type is asserted.

final_claim: For X_n the ordinary matching complex of the graph complement of C_n, the first order n in 3..9 with reduced integral homology nonzero in two nonnegative degrees is n=9: Htilde_2=Z^42, Htilde_3=Z, no other nonzero groups and no torsion in the enumerated interval.
